## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- The sources found do not support this break's listed tide preference.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey or peer-reviewed study of the bottom was found.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | High | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Swell size | Low | Supported by one source (a surf magazine); 1 disagrees. |
| Swell period | Low | Supported by one source (a surf magazine). |
| Wind | High | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Tide | Low | No source supports the listed tide preference; 1 disagrees. |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Moderate | Described by 4 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |
| Season | High | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 3 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Five readable sources from four publishers (Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, WSL x2, Ultimate France). Wind: east is stated by three publishers (Surf-Forecast, WSL, Ultimate France), 5 deg from the profile's 95; all are now read directly. Swell direction: W (Surf-Forecast), W-NW (WSL), W and N (Ultimate France) agree with the profile window. Size conflict: WSL head-high to double overhead+ (about 5-12 ft) against Ultimate France 0.5-2.5 m (about 1.6-8.2 ft, 'holds shape up to 2.5 m'); both overlap the profile's 3-15 ft, but neither supports 15 ft. Period conflict: WSL's 9-12 s ideal is below the profile's 14 s ideal; no other source gives a period. Tide conflict: WSL says any tide at La Gravière; Ultimate France says outgoing tide best, incoming tide closes out and high tide is dead. Neither supports the profile's 'mid' directly; Ultimate France at least rules out high tide. Season: autumn (Surf-Forecast, Ultimate France) and autumn-winter for the region (WSL 2022) all agree; nothing specific to February-March. Sand bottom, dated: WSL 2015 (sandbank, offshore trench), WSL 2022 and Ultimate France 2026 (several good sandbanks). No measured bathymetry. Crossref found Capbreton canyon-head morphobathymetry papers (e.g. Marine Geology 2014, 2020), but none names La Gravière, so none was recorded.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 1.6 ft | documented | S5 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | head high to double overhead+ | documented | S3 | no separate setting; working range 3–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 8.2 ft | documented | S5 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: Ultimate France gives La Gravière a wave size of 0.5 to 2.5 m; 0.5 m x 3.28 = 1.6 ft (it does not say whether this is face or swell height).
  - S5 (Ultimate France (ultimatefrance.com)): “2. La Gravière...Wave size: 0.5 to 2.5 m”
- **Ideal range**: WSL's best-conditions table gives swell height as head-high to double overhead+, a height relative to the surfer with no number in feet.
  - S3 (World Surf League): “Swell Height: Head-high to double overhead+”
- **Maximum suitable**: Ultimate France says La Gravière can hold shape up to 2.5 m and gives a wave size of 0.5 to 2.5 m; 2.5 m x 3.28 = 8.2 ft (scale not stated); WSL's 'double overhead+' is open-ended.
  - S5 (Ultimate France (ultimatefrance.com)): “La Gravière works best on an outgoing tide and can hold shape up to 2.5 metres. On an incoming tide, it's prone to close-outs and at high tide there's nothing to ride.”
  - S5 (Ultimate France (ultimatefrance.com)): “2. La Gravière...Wave size: 0.5 to 2.5 m”

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prime months | Sep, Oct, Nov | documented | S1, S5 | `best_months` Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan, Feb, Mar |

Notes:

- **Prime months**: Surf-Forecast says autumn is the optimum time of year and Ultimate France that autumn has the best swells and top conditions (Hossegor in general); WSL's statement that the biggest swells come in fall and winter is about swell size, not the best season (see swell_sources).
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “The optimum time of year for waves is autumn.”
  - S5 (Ultimate France (ultimatefrance.com)): “Autumn: Best swells, fewer crowds, warm water, top surfing conditions.”
- **Secondary season**: No excerpt states a secondary or shoulder season.
- **Swell sources**: WSL (2022, region-wide) says big North Atlantic swells are filtered through the Bay of Biscay and that the swells producing the biggest waves usually come in fall and winter.
  - S4 (World Surf League): “Thanks to a massive underwater canyon that sits just offshore, big North Atlantic swells are filtered through the Bay of Biscay and slam into the nearshore sandbars.”
  - S4 (World Surf League): “Usually, the swells that produce waves of this magnitude occur during the fall and winter months”
- **Wind patterns**: No excerpt describes seasonal wind patterns at the break.

### Geography

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Break type | beach (sandbar), lefts and rights | documented | S1, S2 | `break_type` beach, `wave_direction` both |
| Orientation | — | not documented | — | nearshore-model shore normal estimated as the centre of the optimal swell direction (295° (WNW)) |
| Exposure | exposed | documented | S1 | no setting |
| Bathymetry | several sandbanks fed by swell gathered by a deep offshore trench (the Capbreton submarine canyon) | documented | S2, S3, S4, S5 | no measured bathymetry (profile derived from the swell windows) |

Notes:

- **Break type**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed sandbar break with waves breaking left and right, and Wikipedia lists Gravière among Hossegor's beach breaks.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Hossegor - La Graviere in Landes is an exposed sandbar break that has reasonably consistent surf.”
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Waves at the sandbar break both left and right.”
  - S2 (Wikipedia): “The Hossegor coast has been one of the few world class surfing locations in Atlantic Europe, with beach breaks at Gravière and La Nord, Les Estagnots.”
- **Orientation**: No excerpt states which way the coast or the break faces.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed sandbar break.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Hossegor - La Graviere in Landes is an exposed sandbar break that has reasonably consistent surf.”
- **Bathymetry**: WSL (2015) gives a sand-bank bottom with a deep trench offshore that gathers the swell, Ultimate France multiple good sandbanks, and Wikipedia and WSL (2022) the underwater canyon offshore; no survey of the sandbanks is cited.
  - S3 (World Surf League): “Bottom: Sand Bank...There's a deep trench offshore that helps gather the swell too.”
  - S5 (Ultimate France (ultimatefrance.com)): “La Gravière continues to be a favourite among surfers offering multiple good sand banks, producing heavy peaks”
  - S2 (Wikipedia): “an underwater canyon thousands of metres deep and hundreds of kilometres long, this creates waves from the ocean on the Landes coast”
  - S4 (World Surf League): “Thanks to a massive underwater canyon that sits just offshore, big North Atlantic swells are filtered through the Bay of Biscay and slam into the nearshore sandbars.”
